executive_assessment.text: Evidence distinguishes fruit-frost exposure south of the Sava/Danube, family-farm sensitivity and national modeled drought/precipitation changes; projections are not observed losses.

The 2014 flood study identifies local warning and support gaps in four municipalities and differentiated reception-centre access/protection risks, including language barriers faced by some evacuated Roma women.
Reported city designs, draft climate-planning work and DRR objectives identify capacities and gaps without establishing completed resilience or peace outcomes.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2015-01-16 reports: In the four municipalities studied, the report found no local protection-and-rescue plans, untrained communities, inaudible sirens, no local radio or television guidance, and warnings reaching few people informally.

Source dated 2015-01-16 reports: The study identifies older and disabled people, single mothers, women living alone and illiterate residents (mostly women and Roma) as vulnerable; it also notes language barriers for evacuated Roma women.

Source dated 2015-01-16 reports: The author warns that isolated, unlit large reception centres without organized support can pose security threats to women because of trafficking, sexual-assault and harassment risks.

Source dated 2025 reports: FY 2025 began ten green-infrastructure, mobility and climate-resilience space designs across Leskovac, Kragujevac, Užice, Niš and Novi Sad; consultations/gender analysis covered safety and access.

Source dated 2025 reports: Niš analysis recommended narrowing General Urban Plan boundaries to the continuous urban area and reducing construction zones against population/land-use projections; Leskovac planning addressed decline and urban-rural links.

Source dated 2025 reports: Two draft analyses supported climate integration in a five-year Action Plan for Serbia’s Sustainable Urban Development Strategy; an urban cycling/greenway study launched in Užice.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 13 of 13 evidence records and 1 of 1 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.

No directly inspected country-specific primary evidence linked a climate-attributed hazard to armed conflict or organized violence; the OSCE's 2014 flood study documents disaster-emergency protection risks but makes no climate attribution.
A search lead on Serbia's historical post-conflict environmental cleanup could not be read because the UN Digital Library PDF returned 403; no findings were inferred from its indexed snippet.
The adaptation programme's projected precipitation-risk classes are territory shares derived from a cited study; they do not identify exposed people, local assets or realized losses.
The OSCE flood study has a 78-person sample across four municipalities and incomplete gender-disaggregated administrative records; its results are event-specific, not nationally representative.
UNDP does not report the reference year or score scale for the INFORM figures and provides no project outcome evaluation on the public page.
World Bank city-planning examples are historical FY2025 reported outputs; initiated design, draft analyses and recommendations are not completed resilience effects.
The regional generic climate-conflict statement is not imported as Serbia-specific FCV evidence.
The protection pathway concerns historical flood-evacuation conditions and potential violence, not observed trafficking/assault rates or a climate-attribution finding.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
